posts.title: Exquisite Style
posts.description: Words seem to offend by too much assertion, and to check the suggestions of his reserve. That reserve was life-long. Loving literature, he never lifted a pen except to write a letter. He was not inarticulate, he was only silent. He had an exquisite style from which to refrain. — Alice Meynell, Remembrance

posts.title: Nadezhda Mandelstam’s Intelligence
posts.description: There are many books one admires, Jon Fosse’s Septology or perhaps Gerald Murnane’s Barley Patch for instance. While reading them, I am excited by their distinctive nature and the formal achievement, but cannot imagine returning to either. Eighty pages into Nadezhda Mandelstam’s Hope Against Hope, I am already anticipating rereading and tracking down its sequel. […]

posts.title: Unneeded Notebooks
posts.description: Every acquired book offers the possibility of entering another’s mind. An empty notebook offers the chance to discover one’s own mind.
